Looks like rmsync failed for every test that didn't close all of its open fds. I _think_ that I've caught all of them.
Given all of the issues encountered, and assuming they were actually fixed, I think that it makes sense to mark this as semver-major.

> Given all of the issues encountered, and assuming they were actually fixed, I think that it makes sense to mark this as semver-major.

@Linkgoron do you have an example of code that works in a current Node.js version and would throw with this PR? Is this something we should document?

> > Given all of the issues encountered, and assuming they were actually fixed, I think that it makes sense to mark this as semver-major.
> 
> @Linkgoron do you have an example of code that works in a current Node.js version and would throw with this PR? Is this something we should document?

The test that I added in ` test/parallel/test-fs-rm.js` doesn't throw in current Node versions, even though it should throw (`rm `already gives an error in the callback). As we've seen with the test fixes, It appears that trying to delete a folder with an open file also throws on Windows and maybe ARM (doesn't throw on Mac or Linux). 

I'm not sure if there's any special documentation needed - in theory, this is just making `rm` and `rmSync` behave the same.

Edit:
Now that I think about it, it might have a stronger effect, as previously it would delete all of the files and only leave those that were errored and now it'll stop when the first error is encountered. This is _similar_ to what happens in the callback version, but not exactly the same as the `cb` versions also emits an error and stops its operation if one `rm` fails, but as it deletes in parallel some might still get deleted before the error is emitted.

https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/57723c29af9a922b95a06c6ca4240e77f2651f02/lib/internal/fs/rimraf.js#L143

https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/57723c29af9a922b95a06c6ca4240e77f2651f02/lib/internal/fs/rimraf.js#L249

Libuv's implementation of `chmod` uses [`NtQueryInformationFile`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/nf-ntifs-ntqueryinformationfile) with the `FileInformationClass` set to [`FileBasicInformation`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/ns-wdm-_file_basic_information) to retrieve the `FileInformation`. Then it updates `FileInformation` with the [`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/file-attribute-constants) mask. Finally, it updates the `FileInformation` of the file using [`NtSetInformationFile`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/nf-ntifs-ntsetinformationfile) with the `FileInformationClass` set to [`FileBasicInformation`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/ns-wdm-_file_basic_information).

So, I think, Libuv's `chmod` works in a way more similar to `attrib` than the way `icacls` works. That's why I think we should check whether this works.

> Libuv's implementation of `chmod` uses [`NtQueryInformationFile`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/nf-ntifs-ntqueryinformationfile) with the `FileInformationClass` set to [`FileBasicInformation`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/ns-wdm-_file_basic_information) to retrieve the `FileInformation`. Then it updates `FileInformation` with the [`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/file-attribute-constants) mask. Finally, it updates the `FileInformation` of the file using [`NtSetInformationFile`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/nf-ntifs-ntsetinformationfile) with the `FileInformationClass` set to [`FileBasicInformation`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/ns-wdm-_file_basic_information).
> 
> So, I think, Libuv's `chmod` works in a way more similar to `attrib` than the way `icacls` works. That's why I think we should check whether this works.

There's already an open issue in Libuv (https://github.com/libuv/libuv/issues/2838) to use ACL in `chmod`. So, I guess it is better to stick to `icacls` till there is a change from Libuv's side.
I think this PR also fixes https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/34580. Could you please add a test to verify it?

issue_context.title: rmSync does not throw error if file exists but cannot be deleted.
issue_context.body:
<!--
Thank you for reporting an issue.

This issue tracker is for bugs and issues found within Node.js core.
If you require more general support please file an issue on our help
repo. https://github.com/nodejs/help


Please fill in as much of the template below as you're able.

Version: output of `node -v`
Platform: output of `uname -a` (UNIX), or output of `"$([Environment]::OSVersion | ForEach-Object VersionString) $(if ([Environment]::Is64BitOperatingSystem) { "x64" } else { "x86" })"` in PowerShell console (Windows)
Subsystem: if known, please specify affected core module name
-->

* **Version**: v14.17.0 and v16.1.0
* **Platform**: Darwin Randalls-iMac.fios-router.home 20.4.0 Darwin Kernel Version 20.4.0: Thu Apr 22 21:46:47 PDT 2021; root:xnu-7195.101.2~1/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64 (macOS 11.3.1)
* **Subsystem**: filesystem

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

`fs.rmSync` does not error if file exists, but cannot be deleted because parent directory is readonly. The file remains, but no error is thrown. (Note that `fs.rm` works as expected.)

I expect the following code to emit an EACCES error, but it does not:
```js
import * as nodefs from 'fs'

nodefs.mkdirSync('tmp')
nodefs.writeFileSync('tmp/file', 'A file.')
nodefs.chmodSync('tmp', '500')
nodefs.rmSync('tmp/file' {force: true})
```

However, this code does emit that error:
```js
import * as nodefs from 'fs'

nodefs.mkdirSync('tmp')
nodefs.writeFileSync('tmp/file', 'A file.')
nodefs.chmodSync('tmp', '500')
nodefs.rm('tmp/file', {force: true}, function(err) {
    if (err) console.error(err)
})
```
as does:
```js
import * as nodefs from 'fs'
import * as promisefs from 'fs/promises'

nodefs.mkdirSync('tmp')
nodefs.writeFileSync('tmp/file', 'A file.')
nodefs.chmodSync('tmp', '500')
promisefs.rm('tmp/file', {force: true})
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Always reproducible.

### What is the expected behavior?

The file is not deleted, and the error is emitted:
```js
[Error: EACCES: permission denied, unlink 'tmp/file'] {
  errno: -13,
  code: 'EACCES',
  syscall: 'unlink',
  path: 'tmp/file'
}
```

### What do you see instead?

The file is not deleted, but no error is emitted.

### Additional information

The commands `mkdir tmp ; touch tmp/file ; chmod 500 tmp ; rm -f tmp/file` show the expected result `rm: tmp/file: Permission denied` and the file is not deleted.

I believe Linux systems also exhibit this, but have not explicitly tested this minimal reproducible example on Linux.
